items.title: Substring match on 'output' silently skips dataset files

findings.title: Substring 'output' filter can hide dataset files
findings.explanation: Any directory whose full path contains the substring "output" is skipped, so a dataset stored under e.g. `/data/outputs_study/` or `/home/user/output/` yields no original files for any patient, and the module reports patients as missing/empty rather than explaining why.
findings.suggestion: Compare against the actual output directory path (e.g. `os.path.join(datasetPath, OUTPUT_FOLDER)`) instead of a substring test.

findings.title: Substring match on 'output' silently skips dataset files
findings.explanation: Concrete failure: a dataset stored under any path that contains 'output' produces no copied originals and no warning.

items.title: ClassAnnotationLib/__init__.py is not installed by CMake

findings.title: ClassAnnotationLib/__init__.py is not installed by CMake
findings.explanation: The repository contains `ClassAnnotationLib/__init__.py`, but it is not listed in MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS, so it is not installed. Imports such as `from ClassAnnotationLib.ClassAnnotationUIUtils import getMainColor` (ClassAnnotation.py:245) currently work only because the directory is added to `sys.path` and Python treats it as a namespace package; if that `sys.path` hack is removed the imports break.
findings.suggestion: Add `${MODULE_NAME}Lib/__init__.py` to MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS and use package-relative imports.

items.title: Deletion path built from user-editable CSV without containment check

findings.title: Deletion path built from user-editable CSV without containment check
findings.explanation: patientID comes from the CSV 'Patient ID' column. A crafted or corrupted value that resolves outside the output tree would cause recursive deletion of that location.

items.title: Empty-directory deletion walks the whole user-chosen output folder

findings.title: Empty-directory deletion walks the whole user-chosen output folder
findings.explanation: `movePatientIfReclassified` iterates over every subdirectory of the user-selected output folder and, if a subdirectory becomes empty, removes it with `shutil.rmtree(currentClassPath)` (line 24). If the user points the output folder at a directory that already contains unrelated (possibly empty) folders, those folders are deleted. Only empty directories are removed, so the harm is limited, but the operation is not restricted to folders the extension created.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the scan to folders matching the `class<N>` naming pattern the module itself creates.

items.title: Errors during copy and CSV read are swallowed

findings.title: Errors during copy and CSV read are swallowed
findings.explanation: Users are not told when the previous classification could not be read, or when copies failed, so reclassification may silently lose track of earlier assignments.

items.title: No automated tests and no sample data

findings.title: No automated tests and no sample data
findings.explanation: The only test registration is commented out, and the module's own `slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)` depends on a unittest class in ClassAnnotation.py that I did not verify. Users and maintainers therefore have no regression coverage for the CSV/folder bookkeeping that this tool relies on, and no sample dataset is provided for trying the module.
findings.suggestion: Add a small synthetic dataset and a test that exercises load → classify → CSV/folder output.

findings.title: No automated tests and no clinical-use disclaimer
findings.explanation: Without tests, regressions in the CSV and folder-reorganisation logic will not be caught by the build.

items.title: Scene is cleared without confirmation when switching label mode

findings.title: Scene is cleared without confirmation when switching label mode
findings.explanation: `generateMultiLabelClassButtons` (line 452) and `setLabelModeFromButtons` (line 778) call `slicer.mrmlScene.Clear(0)` unconditionally, discarding every node in the scene (including unsaved segmentations or measurements the user loaded) without asking. Dataset loading does ask first (line 1635: "Loading a new dataset will clear the scene. Do you want to continue?"), so the inconsistency is easy to hit: a user who has other work open and toggles single/multi-label mode loses it silently.
findings.suggestion: Prompt before clearing, or only remove the nodes this module created (track them and delete those).

items.title: Silent exception swallowing in patient hashing

findings.title: Silent exception swallowing in patient hashing
findings.explanation: `compute_patient_hashes` swallows every read error and returns `[""]` when nothing could be read (line 92). The hash is used for duplicate detection (`isPatientDuplicate`, `markAsDuplicateMulti`), so an unreadable or unsupported file silently yields an empty hash and can make distinct patients look identical or duplicates go undetected, with no message to the user.
findings.suggestion: Report unreadable files to the user (warningDisplay) and skip duplicate comparison when the hash is empty.

items.title: Whole files read into memory for hashing; long work on the GUI thread

findings.title: Whole files read into memory for hashing; long work on the GUI thread
findings.explanation: `f.read()` loads the entire file into memory, and `compute_patient_hashes` additionally converts each volume to a numpy array (`sitk.GetArrayFromImage`) and hashes it. All of this runs synchronously from the widget (no thread, no progress dialog), so loading a large dataset can freeze the Slicer GUI for a long time and can exhaust memory on big files.
findings.suggestion: Hash in chunks, and move dataset scanning/hashing to a `qt.QTimer`-driven or CLI-thread worker with progress reporting.

findings.title: sys.path modified at module import
findings.evidence:
if LIB_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, LIB_DIR)
findings.explanation: Importing the module (which Slicer does at startup for every installed scripted module) prepends the module's ClassAnnotationLib directory to the global `sys.path`. This is a process-wide side effect affecting other extensions and can shadow same-named modules; the module is also imported eagerly rather than lazily.
findings.suggestion: Use a relative import (`from .ClassAnnotationLib...`) or `importlib` with an explicit path instead of mutating `sys.path`.

findings.title: No clinical-use disclaimer in README
findings.evidence: Module for 3D Slicer allowing annotation of medical image datasets.
findings.explanation: The module is aimed at clinicians annotating medical image datasets, but the README contains no statement that it is not a medical device and must not be used for diagnosis. This is informational only, not a gate.
findings.suggestion: Add a short research-use-only / not-for-diagnosis note.
